aiOverview.content: NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California today, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PDT). This marks the safe return of four astronauts after a 10-day, historic mission orbiting the Moon.Key Details for Artemis II Splashdown:Where to Watch: Live coverage is available on NASA's YouTube channel.Location: The Orion capsule will land off the coast of San Diego, California.Visibility: Residents in Southern California might hear a sonic boom between 5:00 p.m. and 5:15 p.m. PDT.Mission Goal: The flight tested systems for future, longer lunar missions.Additional Space Activity:SpaceX Launch: A Falcon 9 rocket is scheduled to launch from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California around 10:39 p.m. ET (7:39 p.m. PDT) on April 10, 2026, roughly 200 miles north of the splashdown site.You can follow the live recovery progress of the Artemis II crew through NASA's blogs. NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California today, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PDT). This marks the safe return of four astronauts after a 10-day, historic mission orbiting the Moon. Key Details for Artemis II Splashdown: Where to Watch: Live coverage is available on NASA's YouTube channel. NASA's YouTube channel Location: The Orion capsule will land off the coast of San Diego, California. Visibility: Residents in Southern California might hear a sonic boom between 5:00 p.m. and 5:15 p.m. PDT. Mission Goal: The flight tested systems for future, longer lunar missions. Additional Space Activity: SpaceX Launch: A Falcon 9 rocket is scheduled to launch from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California around 10:39 p.m. ET (7:39 p.m. PDT) on April 10, 2026, roughly 200 miles north of the splashdown site.
